statement: Every census record of class both carries a recorded classification in scripts/checks/code-navigability-fallback-classification.json, bound to the site's content hash with a reason: named-state-at-owner (the dual path becomes a named state decided once at its owner), documented-default (the schema or constructor guarantee that makes the default inert is cited), or second-authority (two owners answer one fact, an R03 finding routed to a quest of its own); the budget row fallback_sites_unclassified reads zero, and the classifications are verified by an agent other than the one that wrote them.

constraints.statement: A classification is a claim about authority and goes through the verification templates; a documented-default entry cites the guarantee that makes it inert, or it is not a documented default.
An R03 finding is recorded and routed to its owner's quest; it is not edited inline here (R17).
A classification is void when the site's content hash changes; the row counts it unclassified again.
Classification proceeds owner by owner in the epic's order and each batch names the agent that classified and the agent that verified.

Coverage classes identify investigation candidates only. Before deletion or classification, trace the canonical owner, every actual caller/export/dynamic entrypoint and fixture, distinguish legitimate defaults/owned conversion from alternate semantics, and retain discriminating evidence. No observed execution is not proof that code is dead. No legacy, compatibility, fallback or second authority is retained as an exception.

This Quest retains its bounded work under code-navigability-and-mistake-resistance. Coordinate shared owner changes with repository-legacy-fallback-closure (Q11) and Q5 canonical-replica-completion-observation. Classification or routed debt does not close global removal; Q11 requires zero unresolved violations and zero unclassified candidates across maintained executable code. One writer per interaction, with independent owner-sized repairs.
